question: Must Gateway TLS auto-generation continue to support writable configured paths that cannot create hard links, or may OpenClaw require link-capable storage for interruption-safe publication?
rationale: The hard-link design provides strong no-overwrite publication semantics, but it changes the filesystem capabilities required by an existing configuration surface; selecting the permanent compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve configured-path compatibility
options.body: Add and test an interruption-safe no-overwrite publication design for supported filesystems where hard links are unavailable.

options.title: Require link-capable storage
options.body: Keep hard-link-only publication but add explicit preflight validation, actionable diagnostics, upgrade documentation, and cross-platform coverage for the narrower contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve configured-path compatibility
recommendation.body: Add and test an interruption-safe no-overwrite publication design for supported filesystems where hard links are unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recovery implementation and the underlying process-lifecycle refactor, so they are best positioned to choose the intended filesystem contract.
